text_b434f5e85711: While GPS is recording, an electric locomotive shows your last GPS position. The totals above it show running time in green and stopped time in red, both in hours and minutes. text_702b38d037ef: Use “Import Excel” to read an XLSX wagon list. Select G, P or G+P first. Review the preview and apply the values. Wagon count, last vehicle and total row are detected dynamically. Fields 4b and 16b use only the first word of the destination. Results are rounded up at the end. G+P uses the first five wagons in G minus 25%, then P; above 500 m unrounded wagon-train length, P is additionally reduced by 5%. The locomotive uses G−25% once. Missing brake weights are not substituted. Switching G/P/G+P recalculates stored source rows. Manually changing wagon count, length, brake weight or weight detaches automatic import calculation. Save the brake sheet afterwards.
text_a49da6191d99: Use “Add towed locomotive” to add non-working locomotives as wagons. Import the wagon list first. Select the locomotive, a unique position in the entire wagon train, its brake mode, brake weight and destination. For G, explicitly choose count or zero. Check length and weight. Enter the final journey destination and drop-off order; the same station must use the same order number. Fields 4b/16b end at the next drop-off station. Saving creates separate section versions. After each drop-off, positions, first/last vehicle, count, length, weight and braking including G+P deductions are recalculated. Missing values are not estimated. Field 9 includes locomotive numbers and drop-off stations. Open versions with the section buttons. Make changes only in the original brake sheet and save again. Superseded versions disappear from the selector and cannot produce new documents. Previously archived documents are retained.
text_3f681bbb86e6: The import treats numbers as numbers even when Excel stores them as text. Length (D), cargo weight (E), gross weight (F) and brake weights (H/P and I/G) are recalculated from individual wagons. These column totals appear in the preview. E is a check total; F is used for train weight. Columns are identified by their headings. Wagon count and the last data row can vary. Exact individual values are used; only final form values are rounded up. Differing Excel summary cells are shown alongside the recalculated values. Missing G/P values are not replaced with values from the other column. When the selected brake mode does not fit, the preview proposes only a clearly identified G, P or G+P mode. Check the actual brake mode and totals. Only “Apply values” changes field 15 and wagon values. Cancel leaves the form unchanged.
